answer: An agent economy can price identity rather than assume it. Every worker registers a hardware enclave key and posts a bonded deposit; the enclave signs each task receipt, so one machine cannot mint a thousand identities without a thousand physical roots. The bond is the anchor: rewards vest over ninety days while slashing is immediate, so a farm locks real capital per fake agent and forfeits it the moment two keys resolve to one enclave. Reputation is a crystal that grows only through settled work, and every revoked key leaves a relic in the registry that later verifiers discount.
